slides.title: Read it like a detective
content: 3 phrases → 3 questions: from origin…? · blocked by CORS policy…? · No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header…?
each phrase click-revealed

slides.title: Origin = scheme + host + port
content: 📌 Concept 2 · flats in one building — mail for flat 3000 isn't for flat 8000
note: localhost vs 127.0.0.1 = different hosts → different origins; expect surprises

slides.title: Same origin — or not?
content: doc's 3 rows, all No: port differs (our case) · scheme differs · host differs
revealed row-by-row after the class predicts

slides.title: The delivery arrived — the guard won't hand it over
content: 📌 Concept 3 · rows: delivery arrives→Django's 200 · guard checks name→browser checks header · no name→page never sees data
whys: Postman/curl have no guard (why Postman worked) · static API always left the name (why never seen before)

visual.why: the doc's guard analogy as a mapping

slides.title: The error names the missing paperwork
content: header lives on the RESPONSE → responses come from servers → the fix belongs to the server
CORS definition verbatim: response headers by which a server declares 'pages from this origin may read my responses'

slides.title: Teach Django to send the header
content: pip install django-cors-headers
3 edits: app · middleware high · CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS ('the name left at the gate')
checkpoint: same fetch → products; response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin
note — the doc's two predicts, kept as teaching points: Postman works now? yes — it always did (no browser, no guard) · can :5500 read it? no — the guard holds a list of names, not an open gate
